BiblicalUsage: ʻEreb is evening — the dusk that closes the day. There was evening and there was morning, the first day; the Passover lamb was killed in the evening; and the evening sacrifice went up as the day ended. It is the word for the day's close, when work stops and worship rises.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe ʻereb teaches me that God measures days from evening to morning — rest comes before the work, not after it. I hold that the evening sacrifice is the picture of my day: it ends with worship, not with worry.
RelatedEvents: Creation; The Exodus and the Red Sea
